newsitem.title: USA: Tyco to acquire Keystone for $1.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: Tyco to acquire Keystone for $1.2 bln.

text.p: Tyco International Ltd said on Tuesday that it had a definitive agreement to acquire Keystone International Inc in a deal valued at about $1.2 billion.
Under the deal, Keystone, a manufacturer of industrial valves, is to be merged into a Tyco subsidiary. Tyco is a diversified manufacturer of industrial and commercial products.

Keystone shareholders are to receive 0.54183 shares of Tyco stock for each share they own. The transaction is valued at $34 per share to Keystone shareholders, or $1.2 billion, based on Tyco's May 20 closing price of $62.75.

"The combination of Keystone with Tyco's flow control group creates the premier, worldwide company in the valve industry," Tyco chairman and chief executive Dennis Kozlowski said in a statement. "This merger is in line with our strategy of growing our global presence in high value, stable industrial markets."
Keystone has annual revenues of about $700 million.
The transaction, which will be accounted for as a pooling of interests, is expected to close in September, the companies said. The boards both companies have approved the transaction.

The planned Keystone acquisition is the latest in a string of deals put together by Tyco. Recent acquisitions include, Inbrand Corp, a maker of disposable products for adult incontinence; AT&T Corp's underwater telecommunications cable business; and ADT Ltd, an installer and servicer of electronic security systems.
